response.sql: SELECT rating, AVG(length) AS avg_length, AVG(rental_rate / rental_duration) AS avg_rate_per_day FROM film WHERE replacement_cost >= 20.99 GROUP BY rating;

assumptions.assumption: A film is 'expensive' when replacement_cost is at or above 20.99 (the cutoff is inclusive). The request does not settle the boundary.

The per-film rate is rental_rate / rental_duration, computed for each film and then averaged. Missing length values are skipped by AVG. rental_rate and rental_duration are NOT NULL, and rental_duration is 3 to 7 per the verified data, so the division is safe. No rounding is applied.

alternatives.interpretation: The cutoff is strict: a film is expensive only when replacement_cost is strictly above 20.99.
alternatives.sql: SELECT rating, AVG(length) AS avg_length, AVG(rental_rate / rental_duration) AS avg_rate_per_day FROM film WHERE replacement_cost > 20.99 GROUP BY rating;

alternatives.interpretation: The per-film rate is read as a ratio of averages: the average rental_rate divided by the average rental_duration within each rating, rather than an average of per-film ratios.
alternatives.sql: SELECT rating, AVG(length) AS avg_length, AVG(rental_rate) / AVG(rental_duration) AS avg_rate_per_day FROM film WHERE replacement_cost >= 20.99 GROUP BY rating;
